take_homes: Access and absorption are different numbers. Count the people who use the tool, not the people who have a licence.
Ask 'what would have to be true for them to switch?' about one person's actual job before building or rolling out anything.
A plan with polished technical parts and unnamed people is a warning sign. Name the person who owns it.

monday.move: Pick one colleague on my team whose job a tool might help and ask how they do that job today. Write down the answer and nothing else.
monday.who: One director-level peer, or someone in my own business development team
monday.when: Within the week, in a 20-minute slot
monday.stop_condition: If the answer shows they have a working solution they don't want to change, I stop. I run no pilot.
monday.blocker: My calendar is full of steering groups from the last programme, and a colleague may see the question as a rollout in disguise.

misconception.why: The module did not show me anything I couldn't have done two years ago, so 'wait and see' is not really challenged. The author's failed project was candid, though, and the module treats adoption as a human problem with testable steps and not as a belief to take on faith. That is more honest than the last three programmes. I still don't know what the agents do that is new.

one_line: Surprisingly honest about why rollouts stall and the switch question is useful, but every third slide is a generic 'involve stakeholders' filler and I never saw a demo of what is actually new.
